messages.author: 5dadf4dbf792b603
messages.subject: model fit and item loadings decrease when additional predictors (OVs) are added into the SEM model
parts:
Dear all,

I fitted the following two SEM models. The difference between the two models: In model 2, there are three additional predictors (observed variables: ADM.st.y, RIV.st.y, NS.st.y) in the regression.
What puzzles me is that the model fit of model 2 is considerably lower. I inspected the two models and the loadings of the STAI items are lower in the second model. It seems like the STAI items correlate with the additional predictors (ADM.st.y, RIV.st.y, NS.st.y) and thus their loadings on the latent trait STAI.women and the model fit decreases. I ran residuals() but it only gives the residual associations between the STAI and NARQ items but not the residuals between the additional predictors and the items. Any idea what is going on here and how I could improve the model fit?

Model 1
STAI.RIV.model<- '

riv_d.x =~ narq13.x + narq14.x + narq17.x
riv_s.x =~ narq6.x+ narq9.x + narq10.x
riv_a.x =~ narq4.x + narq11.x + narq12.x
RIV.men =~ riv_s.x+riv_d.x+riv_a.x
STAI.women =~ STAI4.y+ STAI2.y+ STAI3.y+ STAI1r.y+ STAI5.y+ STAI6r.y+ STAI7r.y+ STAI8.y+ STAI9.y+ STAI10r.y+ STAI11.y+ STAI12.y+ STAI13r.y+ STAI14.y+ STAI15.y+ STAI16r.y+ STAI17.y+ STAI18.y+ STAI19r.y+ STAI20.y
RIV.men ~ STAI.women'

STAI.RIV.fit <- sem(STAI.RIV.model,Couples,meanstructure=T,zero.cell.warn=F,std.lv=TRUE)

Model 2
STAI.RIV.model<- '

riv_d.x =~ narq13.x + narq14.x + narq17.x
riv_s.x =~ narq6.x+ narq9.x + narq10.x
riv_a.x =~ narq4.x + narq11.x + narq12.x
RIV.men =~ riv_s.x+riv_d.x+riv_a.x
STAI.women =~ STAI4.y+ STAI2.y+ STAI3.y+ STAI1r.y+ STAI5.y+ STAI6r.y+ STAI7r.y+ STAI8.y+ STAI9.y+ STAI10r.y+ STAI11.y+ STAI12.y+ STAI13r.y+ STAI14.y+ STAI15.y+ STAI16r.y+ STAI17.y+ STAI18.y+ STAI19r.y+ STAI20.y
RIV.men ~ STAI.women+ADM.st.y+RIV.st.y+NS.st.y'

STAI.RIV.fit <- sem(STAI.RIV.model,Couples,meanstructure=T,zero.cell.warn=F,std.lv=TRUE)

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: model fit and item loadings decrease when additional predictors (OVs) are added into the SEM model
parts:
Michael—

     Fixing residual variances makes the single indicator factor models identified.  Also remember that the lavaan:::sem function has defaults.  If you run the same model using lavaan:::lavaan, it may fail the identification check.  The parTable function might clarify exactly which parameters were estimated under each different specification.

     Observed variable predictors may be modeled either as random variables with random sampling error or as “fixed-x” variables.  If treated as “fixed-x,” the rules change substantially.  Ask for residuals and the model-implied covariance matrix to see the difference.  A variable cannot be “fixed-x” if it is dependent, so treating those variables as indicators of factor achieved the same thing as “fixed.x=F”, and fixing residual variances at 0 made factor and indicator identical.

--Ed Rigdon
